questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Restriction Endonucleases' refers to.
questions.a: Molecular scissors that read a specific palindromic stretch of double-stranded DNA and slice each backbone at a set point within it.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Restriction Endonucleases'.
questions.a: Molecular scissors that cut DNA at specific recognition sites, often leaving sticky ends.

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Gel Electrophoresis and Elution' refers to.
questions.a: A technique used to separate negatively charged DNA fragments by size using an electric field through an agarose gel matrix, followed by extraction of the desired band.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Gel Electrophoresis and Elution'.
questions.a: Sieving effect of agarose separates DNA fragments; smaller fragments move faster toward the anode.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Isolation of Genomic DNA'.
